name: Alan Auerbach
current_role: Founder, Chairman, CEO and President, Puma Biotechnology (NASDAQ: PBYI)
profile: Biomedical engineer turned biotech analyst turned founder. He founded Cougar Biotechnology in 2003, whose prostate-cancer drug abiraterone (Zytiga) led to J&J's ~$1bn acquisition in 2009, then founded Puma Biotechnology in 2010, which commercialises the breast-cancer drug neratinib (Nerlynx).
interesting_fact: Cougar's lead drug abiraterone acetate, licensed in as an early-stage asset, was approved for metastatic prostate cancer in the US in April 2011 after J&J bought Cougar in 2009.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Cougar he was a biotech sell-side analyst (Wells Fargo Securities, Seidler Companies) and was ranked second in the NASDAQ/Starmine survey of analyst stock-picking performance in biotechnology; earlier he designed oncology clinical trials at Diagnostic Products Corp. He holds BS/MS degrees in biomedical engineering (Boston University, USC).
notes: Best route is via Puma IR (Mariann Ohanesian, Senior Director IR). Biotech focus, limited overlap with energy/data centers.

name: Xie Yi
current_role: Chairman, CEO and controlling shareholder, Suzhou Tianmai Thermal Technology (SZSE: 301626)
profile: Xie Yi founded Suzhou Tianmai in 2007 with his wife Shen Fenghua; it makes thermal-management parts (heat pipes, vapor chambers, synthetic graphite films) for customers such as CATL, Huawei and Samsung. The company listed in Shenzhen in 2024 raising $87m; he directly owns ~40.8% and in 2026 the company was issuing convertible bonds to expand.
interesting_fact: He started his first job at 16 at a local factory making thermal-management products, the same niche he later built a billionaire-scale company in.
notes: Low public profile, no English-language interviews found. Thermal management for electronics/batteries is relevant to data-center cooling. Reach via the securities affairs office (zq@ email from the 2026 half-year report); Chinese-language outreach advisable.
